title: Intake decision ledger and deprecation safeguards for open-model onboarding
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: New open-model submissions into the catalog lack a structured record of intake decisions (why a model/variant was accepted, pinned, or rejected), and we currently lack a standard deprecation/fallback policy for unpinned community variants. This creates risk for runtime regressions, surprise behavior after upstream updates, and operational churn when variants diverge from supported kernels or quantization paths.

Goal: Define a lightweight "decision ledger" and explicit deprecation/safeguard rules that are enforced during model intake and surfaced in the catalog entry + onboarding UI. The ledger should capture acceptance rationale, runtime compatibility signals, pin policy, and a deprecation trigger list. The policy must be implementable with a mix of human checks and automated gates (runtime unit tests, performance deltas, kernel mismatches).
acceptance_criteria: Every new open-model catalog entry created by intake includes a Decision Ledger section with: intake_date, reviewer(s), summary_rationale (1-3 sentences), compatibility_tag(s), pin_policy (pinned/unpinned/soft-pin), and rollback_triggers (list).
The console model detail page renders the Decision Ledger and highlights pin_policy and rollback_triggers clearly for PM/SE/Support users.

A machine-readable compatibility_metadata blob is attached to the model entry with a stable schema (model_architecture, supported_seq_lengths, quantization_profiles, required_kernels), and automated intake tests validate declared fields before Admission moves to 'Approved'.

If a new variant is unpinned, it must pass an automated sanity suite (latency within X% of baseline, perplexity/regression threshold on canary prompt set) before being published to the public catalog; failures surface as 'experimental' and require a manual approval step.

Define deprecation triggers (e.g., kernel mismatch, sustained 5%+ quality regression on monitored prompt sets, third-party license change, or CVE-level vulnerabilities) and an automated notification + rollback plan that can be executed by platform operators.
All decisions are traceable: Decision Ledger entries include links to the PRD/PR/test-run dashboard and a single-source-of-truth artifact (Drive doc or GitHub PR) for future audits.

Engineering has a clear, implementable checklist and API contract for ingesting Decision Ledger fields and compatibility_metadata; a stub API exists in the intake service and passes a minimal e2e test.

decisions_log: 2026-03-05: Decided ledger will be minimal by default: 5 required fields + opt-in free-text rationale to reduce friction.
2026-03-07: Agreed on three pin states: pinned, soft-pin (auto-fallback enabled), unpinned. Soft-pin requires weekly regression monitoring.
2026-03-10: Rejected heavy-weight governance (no full change-board) for community models; will use automated gates + targeted manual review for exceptions.
2026-03-12: Chose baseline sanity-suite: 50 representative prompts, latency SLA, and a small quality regression threshold (configurable per-model).
tradeoffs: Minimal ledger reduces onboarding friction but may hide nuance — mitigated by links to artifacts and optional expanded rationale fields.
Tight automated gates reduce operational surprises but increase false positives; will iterate thresholds in first two cycles.
Pinning policy simplicity (3 states) is less expressive than a fine-grained policy matrix, but easier to reason about for support and customers.
